snapshot.capital_scaled: ₹50 lakh–2 crore for content, a product team and marketing
snapshot.margin_d2c: 60–80% gross margin on digital courses and subscriptions
snapshot.margin_production: Schools and institutions pay less per student but buy in bulk
snapshot.distribution_note: Parents and schools are hard to reach; trust and results sell

tailwinds: Parents spend heavily on education, even in smaller towns.
Cheap smartphones and data let students learn online anywhere.
AI makes personalised learning and content creation cheaper.
The National Education Policy pushes skills, coding and early learning.
headwinds: Byju's collapse and aggressive sales tactics damaged trust in edtech.
Free content on YouTube competes with paid courses.
Student engagement drops quickly after sign-up.
Schools buy slowly and pay late.
angle_2026: After the edtech boom and bust, parents and schools are wary of big promises. In 2026, edtech startups that grow focus on one clear outcome, like reading, spoken English or a specific exam, prove results, and sell honestly instead of pushing loans and long contracts.
cost_basis: Estimated for a small team building a learning product for one age group or outcome, 2026 prices.

setup_costs.covers: App or web platform, or a no-code version

unit_economics.note: Completion rates decide renewals and referrals. Students who finish recommend you; those who drop out don't.

investor_probes: What share of students complete the course?
How much does it cost to win a student?
Why pay for this when YouTube is free?
bootstrap_takeaway: Start with live classes for a small group, prove results, then turn what works into recorded content and software.
licences: Privacy policy and parental consent for children's data under the Digital Personal Data Protection Act
Compliance with the consumer protection guidelines on online education

hard_truths.title: Trust is low
hard_truths.text: After edtech scandals, parents are sceptical. Offer free trials and honest refund policies.

hard_truths.title: Engagement drops
hard_truths.text: Most students stop after the first few weeks. Live elements and progress tracking help.

hard_truths.title: Free content
hard_truths.text: YouTube offers much for free. You need structure, feedback and results.

hard_truths.title: Schools are slow
hard_truths.text: School sales take months. Plan for long cycles.

plan_goal: The aim is 100 paying students, with at least 60% completing.

plan.title: Pick one outcome
steps: Choose one age group and one result.

plan.title: Pilot
steps: Run a live pilot with 10–20 students.

plan.title: Sell
steps: Partner with 3 schools or coaching centres.
